title: Creadoras de Éxito
tagline: Bilingual SaaS platform. Sole developer and architect, concept to production.
description: A bilingual Spanish and English SaaS platform for direct sales leaders to manage their consultant teams and improve retention. Built and shipped alone, from architecture through production deployment and ongoing operations.
overview: A bilingual Spanish and English SaaS platform for direct sales leaders to manage their consultant teams and improve retention. Built and shipped alone, from architecture through production deployment and ongoing operations.
architectureSummary: A full-stack application across three repositories using a contracts-first pattern, where shared TypeScript contracts enforce type safety from the API through to the frontend at compile time. The frontend is a Nuxt 4 single page application on Cloudflare Pages, with the API running on Cloudflare Workers and Supabase handling Postgres and authentication with row-level security. The serverless architecture holds infrastructure cost near flat as the user base grows, which matters for a product sold to individual team leaders rather than enterprises.

decisions.title: Calendar sync that reconciles rather than replaces
decisions.text: Schedule data is the product's core asset, so the sync resolves recurring series back to their root by base ID and preserves record identity across updates instead of deleting and re-creating. Corrupting a director's calendar once would end the customer relationship.

decisions.title: Serverless over managed servers
decisions.text: Edge compute and a managed Postgres backend mean no fixed infrastructure spend and no operational floor to cover before the product is profitable.

decisions.title: Guardrails after the incident, not just a fix
decisions.text: A production outage traced to a server-side bundle exceeding the edge platform's size limit produced no application-level logs. After resolving it, I added bundle size checks to CI so the failure class cannot recur silently.

decisions.title: Domain values live in the contracts, not the schema
decisions.text: Enum-like columns on the CRM tables carry no database CHECK constraints. Allowed values are defined once in the shared Zod contracts, so extending a picklist is a TypeScript change rather than a migration. Field types that map directly to code paths keep their constraints, since those need a code change anyway.

technicalApproach: Owned production infrastructure directly: deployments, database schema management, DNS across two custom domains, secret rotation, and staging parity
outcome: Built and shipped alone, from architecture through production deployment and ongoing operations. The serverless architecture keeps infrastructure cost near flat as the user base grows.
